engagement_title: Voltcast episode 42 channel delivery: shorten a twelve minute review into a highlight that keeps the sounds the review is about, reframe it for every feed without enlarging it, and build a thumbnail and a card set that hold the channel bug at the size it actually prints
vertical: Music, film, publishing and media. Independent consumer-tech review channel, sponsor-funded, publishing several times a week to a long-form feed plus vertical and square shorts (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, 'Tech Channel Video Editor Needed', from an independent consumer-tech review channel that publishes 'several times a week', needs 'both long-form reviews (8-12 minutes) and short vertical cuts for YouTube Shorts, Reels and TikTok', wants 'a 16:9 master ... plus a reformatted 9:16 or 1:1 version', supplies '4K footage, screen recordings, b-roll and a rough talking-head guide', and asks for thumbnails and channel branding that read on-brand across the grid. The channel, host, episode and every product in it are invented and IP-clean; Voltcast and Voltcast Media are coined. The posted job reads as a cutting job, which is what made the earlier version of this task sit almost entirely on one surface. The fuller commission the same client genuinely needs is the one the post's own last clause implies: the thumbnail and the on-screen furniture are what the grid is judged on, and they have to read as the same channel as the video. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest, because HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is the only form in which a channel publishing several times a week can actually reuse a card set instead of rebuilding it.
client_one_liner: Episode 42 is a power station shootout, half the review is people listening to how loud these things get, and I need it cut down and reformatted for three feeds by Thursday without the sponsor noticing that the shorts look like a different channel.
client_brief:
Voltcast, episode 42 delivery

I run a consumer tech review channel out of Portland. Two of us. We publish several times a week and roughly a third of the revenue is sponsor money, so the grid has to look like one channel and the sponsor's name has to be right.

Episode 42 is a three way portable power station shootout, twelve minutes, and it is finished. What I need is everything that comes after it.

A short version for the feed, cut down from the master rather than re-edited. Then the same short reformatted upright for phones and square for the feeds that want square. Not stretched, not blown up.

The audio is the part I care about most. A lot of this episode is me saying listen to this and then holding the mic to the thing while the fan ramps up or the inverter starts whining. That is the review. The narration itself is not clean, the room has a fridge in it and I moved the mic partway through, so it needs help. Just do not clean it into something that sounds like a podcast.

A thumbnail. I have the scene selects the editor exported. One of them is me holding the middle unit against the studio wall and that is the shot I want, cut out and dropped on our accent colour.

And the on-screen cards, the sponsor read, the spec callouts, the end card, in a file I can open and change next week when the next episode goes up, because right now I rebuild them from scratch every time.

Our bug goes on everything. It is small. Make sure it still looks like our bug when it is small.

Sponsor copy is attached and the disclosure line runs word for word. Plus tell me what you did, because I have to do this again on Monday.
price_band_and_audience: An ad and sponsor-funded independent review channel with a mid six-figure subscriber base, where a sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The band is load-bearing: at this level the look has to read as a credible independent reviewer, confident and plain, with real product photography, restrained on-screen furniture and type that sits out of the way of the thing being reviewed. Push it up into broadcast-grade motion design, glossy sweeps and a full lower-third package and the channel stops reading as independent, which is the entire reason its audience trusts a shootout. Push it down into raw phone-shot energy with mismatched cards and the sponsor does not renew, which is the stated commercial risk. The same three products covered by a manufacturer's own marketing channel would correctly look glossier and more produced, and shipping that treatment here reads as an advertorial. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,600 dollars per episode package.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2020 in Portland, Oregon. A two-person operation with a mid six-figure subscriber base, publishing several times a week.
brand_identity.about: Voltcast is an independent consumer-tech review channel run by two people out of Portland. We buy or borrow the gear, run it hard, and say what we actually think. Episodes go out long-form to the main feed plus vertical and square shorts. About a third of the revenue is sponsor money, so the grid has to look like one channel and the sponsor read has to be exactly right.
brand_identity.audience: Enthusiast buyers and everyday shoppers who want an honest verdict before they spend. They follow us because we are not the manufacturer, and they can tell the difference.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-tier creator economy. A sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The channel has to read as a credible independent reviewer, never as broadcast gloss and never as raw phone-shot filler.
brand_identity.typography: A sturdy grotesque sans for headings and callouts, paired with a clean readable sans for body and specs. Type stays out of the way of the product being reviewed. Spec numbers read cleanly at small sizes.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, dry, and unhyped. We talk like a person who has actually used the thing. Sponsor copy runs as written and the disclosure line is exact. We never oversell.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The channel bug exists only as a flat export on white and we have no editable brand kit. On-screen cards get rebuilt from scratch every episode, which is the problem we want solved. We need the bug prepared as reusable artwork and the card set delivered as a file we can reopen and change each week.
brand_identity.values: Independence from the manufacturers we cover, honesty about what we tested, consistency across the grid, and respect for the audience that trusts the verdict.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_e42_master.mp4 (12 minutes, 4K, finished long-form episode)
assets_supplied.kind: The finished long-form review as published, narration and product sound interleaved, exported from the channel's own edit.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The episode as it went out. It is done, I just need everything that comes after it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The passages the host most wants in the short are the ones where the narration stops and the product's own fan ramp, relay click and inverter whine carry the segment, and those sounds are the review's evidence rather than its background. Separately the narration was recorded across a mic move partway through the episode, so the second half sits at a different distance and level from the first, and one treatment applied across the whole file resolves one half at the other's expense.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_e42_selects/ (12 still frames exported from the timeline)
assets_supplied.kind: Scene selects the editor exported while cutting: product shots, the host holding each unit, two bench overheads and a spec-screen grab.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The selects the editor pulled. The one of me holding the middle unit against the wall is the thumbnail shot."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The chosen holding shot has the unit's light grey chassis against a bright grey studio wall at almost the same value along the top edge and the carry handle, so a subject knockout returns a clean, complete, entirely plausible cutout that has quietly bitten the handle and the top corner, invisible at preview scale and visible only once the cutout sits on the channel's accent colour. Separately the selects were exported at delivery scale rather than at camera scale, so they sit well below the master's frame size, two of the twelve are the same setup a second apart, and one is soft.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_bug.png (channel bug, flat export on white)
assets_supplied.kind: The channel bug: a monoline bolt inside a hexagon with a hairline counter around the bolt and a thin outer ring, exported flat on white at a generous canvas size.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our bug. It goes on everything. It is always small."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The bug traces cleanly and looks perfect at canvas size, but the hairline counter around the bolt and the gap between the bolt and the inner edge of the hexagon are thinner than they appear, and at the size the bug actually sits on a card, on the channel's dark card ground, those counters close and the bug reads as a filled hexagon. Nothing about the file at full size predicts it.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_sponsor_readout.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The sponsor's cleared copy for the read and the cards, including the disclosure line and a short brand note.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Sponsor copy. The disclosure line runs word for word, that is contractual."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The brand note asks for the sponsor's name to be set in a named typeface by family name only, and a family-name lookup on this library returns an arbitrary style rather than the regular cut, so taking the returned name straight through ships the sponsor's name in an italic or a decorative layer face with no error anywhere. The disclosure line is also considerably longer than every other card line, so a card measure chosen from the short lines will not hold it.

assets_supplied.name: voltcast_channel_notes.md
assets_supplied.kind: The host's own notes: the accent colour by name, the three products with their model designations, the episode's verdict order, and which segments he thinks matter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My notes. The accent colour is the orange we always use."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The verdict order in the notes disagrees with the order the products are actually ranked in the finished master, and the notes name four segments as the ones that matter while the episode contains only three of them, so a short or a card set built from the notes alone contradicts the episode it is promoting.

acceptance_bar: The short is genuinely cut down from the master rather than re-edited, and the upright and square versions are reframed from that short rather than cut separately.

The passages where the review is about how a product sounds still contain the product sound, at a level where a viewer can hear what the host is asking them to hear. A short that sounds cleaner but has nothing to listen to is a fail.
The narration is even across the whole short despite the mic move, without either half sounding processed against the other.
No delivered video or still exceeds its source in frame size and nothing is brought up to a delivery size by enlargement, including the upright and square reframes and the thumbnail.
The thumbnail cutout holds its edge on the carry handle and the top corner when it sits on the accent colour at full size, not only at preview scale.
The bug still reads as the bolt inside the hexagon at the size it actually sits on a card, on the channel's dark card ground, with its counters open.
The bug is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, and no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it.
The card set is one working file carrying every card, each canvas keeping its own size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from, and the words are live text the host can retype.

The sponsor's disclosure line appears word for word, complete and legible, on the card it belongs on, and the sponsor's name is set in the intended cut of the intended family rather than whatever a name lookup happened to return.
The published stills read as one channel laid out in a grid: one white point, one black point, one crop logic, with any select that cannot join the set named rather than shipped at eighty percent.

The note records what the short kept and what it dropped, what was done to the audio and where, every resize any tool reported, the disagreement between the notes and the episode, and anything the host should know about using the bug small.

adobe_surfaces.tools: video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole motion half. It reads twelve minutes of finished episode to establish what it actually contains and in what order, shortens the master into the feed cut rather than reassembling it, treats a narration recorded across a mic move by handling the halves separately, and re-aspects the short upright and square from whatever frame size the cut itself returned, never enlarging to reach a feed's native size.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The thumbnail and the still work. It triages twelve timeline selects for which can carry a thumbnail at all, brings the publishable stills to one channel look, cuts the holding shot off a wall that shares its value, composites onto the channel accent, and prepares the bug for reproduction, where the raster preparation is the only lever the tracing tool gives you and the vector hygiene is not performed for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The card set as one native editable document carrying the sponsor read, the spec callouts and the end card at the canvas sizes the long-form and vertical feeds each use, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free-form fixed-canvas layout and the only reason the host stops rebuilding cards from scratch every episode. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the bug goes in as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized wrapper, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), find_fonts, font_styles, font_details, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the cards and the thumbnail, plus the sponsor's named face. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's art direction and has to land on credible independent reviewer rather than broadcast package. A family-name lookup returns an arbitrary style rather than the regular cut, the numeric weight is non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one clean surface the selects do not contain, a plain workbench ground for the end card and the spec callouts, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded and chosen for whether it can be brought to the same target as the channel's own stills. The Boards half persists the thumbnail and card options the host and the sponsor sign off from, placed within the per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cut and the reframes are motion work, the thumbnail is raster work, and the cards have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the host publishes several times a week and needs to reopen them. The brief pins the destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the master, the twelve selects, the bug and the sponsor copy through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which select.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Summarise the master to establish what the episode actually contains and in what order, then read that against the host's notes.
trajectory.judgement: The notes are the host's memory of his own episode, not a record of it. Where the notes and the episode disagree, the episode wins, and saying so is part of the job rather than a correction to make silently.
trajectory.produces: A segment inventory with the verdict order and a written note of every point where the host's notes and the episode disagree.

trajectory.action: Treat the narration audio, handling the two halves either side of the mic move as two passes rather than one, and listen back across the join.
trajectory.judgement: One treatment applied across a file recorded at two mic distances resolves one half at the other's expense. Evenness is judged at the join and at the sponsor read, not on the file's average.
trajectory.produces: A treated narration bed with a per-half parameter log and a note on how the join sits.

trajectory.action: Listen to the treated result specifically at the segments where the review is about how a product sounds, and judge whether the thing the host is pointing at is still there.
trajectory.judgement: Cleaner is not the goal. The only test that matters is whether a viewer told to listen to this can hear it.
trajectory.produces: A written verdict per demonstration segment on whether the product sound survived the treatment.

trajectory.action: Build the feed short by shortening the master, then look at what came back against the segment inventory and the verdict order.
trajectory.judgement: The short is a reduction, not an assembly, and the tool decides which passages survive. A short that promotes a verdict the episode does not reach is worse than a short that runs a little long.
trajectory.produces: A feed short at the target length with a written account of which segments it holds.

trajectory.action: Reframe the short upright and square from the short itself, at or below the frame size it came back at, and check what each framing leaves in shot.
trajectory.judgement: The re-aspect ceiling is set by what the cut actually returned rather than by the 4K master, and enlarging to reach a feed's native size is not an option. Upright framing on a three way shootout decides whether the viewer can still see all three units.
trajectory.produces: An upright version and a square version, each at a size no larger than its source, with the reframing decisions recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview all twelve selects and triage them: which are duplicates, which is soft, what frame size each actually is, and which can carry a thumbnail at the destination size without being enlarged.
trajectory.judgement: The host has already chosen his thumbnail shot. Whether that select can reach the thumbnail size, and whether the wall behind it will let the subject be cut, are two different questions and neither is answered by the host's preference.
trajectory.produces: A per select triage note covering duplication, sharpness, frame size and headroom for the thumbnail crop.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, then bring the publishable selects to one channel target with a call each, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop, and the grid is what the channel is judged on, so the target is a set rather than a run of individually good frames.
trajectory.produces: A graded still set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the host and the unit out of the chosen holding shot and composite onto the channel accent, then inspect the result at full size along the top edge and through the carry handle rather than at preview scale.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout on a subject that shares its value with the wall behind it returns something clean, complete and wrong. The accent ground is where a bite becomes a notch, so that is where it has to be looked at.
trajectory.produces: A thumbnail cutout on the accent ground plus a transparent variant, with the edge inspected at full size.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the plain workbench ground the selects do not contain, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the surface whose existing light can be brought to the channel target, not the most attractive thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale ground frame graded into the channel's world.

trajectory.action: Prepare and trace the bug: word the selection at ink level, set the polarity, crop from the selection's own returned bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox and remove the opaque full canvas ground path.
trajectory.judgement: The tracing tool takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation. Polarity is the whole difference between a mark and a black box, and both outcomes report success.
trajectory.produces: A transparent, scalable bug with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, launder the sponsor's named family and every other name into canonical form and read what each name actually resolved to, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: A family-name lookup on this library hands back an arbitrary style, so the returned name has to be read rather than passed through. The pairing is the agent's own art direction, judged against a credible independent reviewer rather than a broadcast package, and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, style, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight recorded per role, including what the sponsor's named family resolved to.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML carrying the sponsor read card, the spec callouts and the end card at their respective canvas sizes, inlining every photograph as image data, placing the bug as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declaring family and weight on every text element, and setting the card measure from the longest line rather than the shortest.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The disclosure line is the line the measure has to be built around, because it is the one line that cannot be shortened.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole card set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the HTML and export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at card one, and parse the returned per-card markup for every other card and for the bug on each of them.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. The bug appears on every card, so it is the element whose behaviour has to be checked on all of them rather than on the one that renders.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first card, and a per-card markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the sign-off board, add the thumbnail options, the graded stills and the licensed ground within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success, and the vector bug is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note is what stops the host rebuilding this from scratch on Monday.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the speech treatment took out along with the room. Roughly a third of this episode is the host holding a microphone to a machine while a fan ramps, a relay clicks and an inverter whines, and a speech model treats every one of those as noise around the voice. The call succeeds, returns a genuinely cleaner and more professional-sounding file, and the parameters were applied exactly as asked. The loss is audible in one place only, at the moment the host says listen to this and there is nothing there, and which demonstration segments lose their evidence and which survive depends on how each machine's sound overlaps the voice, which is not knowable from the file, its properties or the tool's response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the narration genuinely does need treatment and the demonstration segments are interleaved with it rather than separable in advance, and there is no parameter that says preserve the machine. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the room has a fridge in it and asks not to end up sounding like a podcast, which is the client's taste, not a disclosure that a speech tool removes the review's evidence. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the answer is a different route: treat only the narration-carrying passages and leave the demonstration passages at source, which changes what the short is assembled from and forces the level match to be judged at every boundary between the two.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the audio as two populations rather than one file, treat the narration passages and leave the demonstration passages untouched, re-judge evenness at every join between them, and then re-derive the short and both reframes from the rebuilt bed rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A polished short in which the host repeatedly tells a sponsor-funded audience to listen to how loud these get over silence, on a channel whose credibility is the product it sells.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the thumbnail cutout actually holds its edge. The host's chosen select has a light grey chassis and a carry handle against a bright grey studio wall at almost the same value along the top edge, and a subject knockout on that frame returns a clean, complete, entirely plausible cutout with no error, no warning and no tradeoff entry. Against white or against the pale preview background it looks correct. The bite in the handle and the notch in the top corner only appear once the cutout is sitting on the channel's saturated accent colour at full size, which is the only place it will ever be seen. Whether it bites at all, and how far, is a property of that specific frame's exposure against that specific wall.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: the only way to learn whether a subject separates from a ground it shares a value with is to cut it and put it on the ground it is going to. (b) Nothing states it: the brief names the shot the host wants and says to drop it on the accent colour, which is the client's art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: select the wall by its own material properties, invert, and fill rather than asking for a subject knockout, or abandon the host's chosen select for one where the subject separates, which changes what the thumbnail is and has to be explained back to him.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the thumbnail through a material-named ground selection inverted and filled instead of a subject knockout, or move to a different select and justify the change, then re-composite on the accent, re-inspect the top edge and the handle at full size, and re-derive any card that carried the same cutout.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A thumbnail published to the grid with a notch chewed out of the product's carry handle, on the one asset the channel's click-through and its sponsor renewal both depend on.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the traced bug still reads as the bug at the size it actually reproduces. The trace is clean at canvas size and inspecting it there shows the bolt, the hexagon, the hairline counter and the outer ring all intact. What cannot be known without placing it is that the counter around the bolt and the gap to the inner edge of the hexagon are thinner than they appear at full size, and at the size the bug sits on a card, on the channel's dark card ground, those counters close and the bug reads as a filled hexagon with a smudge in it. The tracing tool takes no options at all, so nothing about the call can be tuned, and the returned artwork is correct by every structural test.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because behaviour at reproduction size against a specific ground is not a property of the trace and cannot be read off the artwork. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the bug is always small and asks that it still look like the bug when it is small, which is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure that this particular trace closes up. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the answer is a different chain: re-prepare the raster the trace is made from so the counters survive, since raster preparation is the only lever the tracing tool has, or place a knocked-out raster at card scale instead of vector, or reconstruct the bug's geometry directly as inline SVG at proportions that hold, each of which changes what is delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation, re-derive the trace from a differently prepared plate or reconstruct the geometry, re-place it at true card size on the dark ground, re-judge it there rather than at canvas size, and re-author and re-export the card set around whichever form survives.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card set in which the channel bug, which sits on every card the channel publishes several times a week, has quietly become a filled hexagon, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Voltcast E42 short with treated audio, plus upright and square
deliverables.spec: One feed short genuinely shortened from the twelve minute master, promoting the verdict the episode actually reaches, plus an upright version and a square version each reframed from that short at or below its frame size with all three units still readable. Carried on a treated audio bed in which the narration is even across the mic move and the demonstration passages still contain the product sound the host is pointing at. Delivered with a written account of what the short kept, what it dropped and what was done to the audio where.

deliverables.name: Voltcast episode still set
deliverables.spec: The publishable selects brought to one channel target (one white point, one black point, one crop logic) so the episode's stills sit in the grid as one channel, plus one licensed camera-scale ground frame graded into the same world. Duplicates and the soft frame identified rather than shipped, and a per frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Voltcast E42 thumbnail, accent ground and transparent
deliverables.spec: The host and unit cut from the studio wall and composited on the channel accent colour at the thumbnail's destination size with no enlargement, the edge holding along the top and through the carry handle when viewed at full size on the accent rather than at preview scale, plus a genuinely transparent variant for reuse on other grounds, with the returned tradeoff record kept for each.

deliverables.name: Voltcast channel bug as placeable artwork
deliverables.spec: The bug delivered as scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, counters open, and reading as the bolt inside the hexagon at the size it actually sits on a card on the channel's dark ground and on the accent colour. Delivered with a stated minimum reproduction size and, where the vector will not hold, an honest alternative form for the smallest placements.

deliverables.name: Voltcast card set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying the sponsor read card, the spec callouts and the end card, each root keeping its own canvas size for the long-form and vertical feeds, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the bug as real vector shapes on every card, photography carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, the sponsor's name in the intended cut of the intended family, and the disclosure line complete and legible word for word. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half, since the host reopens this every episode.

deliverables.name: Delivery note and sign-off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what the short kept and dropped, the audio decisions per passage and per half of the mic move, every resize any tool reported with the asset it applied to, the disagreement between the host's notes and the episode as published, what the sponsor's named family actually resolved to, and the bug's minimum reproduction size with what to use below it. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the thumbnail options, the graded stills and the licensed ground with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.how: Read the duration of every delivered piece from its container metadata: assert the feed short's duration is strictly less than the master's, and assert the upright (9:16) and square (1:1) versions each equal the feed short's duration to within one frame (<= 1/24 s, the master being 24 fps), against the parent the manifest names for each.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered video exceeds the frame size of the piece it derives from and no delivered still exceeds its source select's pixel dimensions.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel frame dimensions of every delivered file from metadata and compare each against the source named in the manifest: assert no delivered still exceeds its source select's dimensions of 1920x1080, and assert each delivered video's frame size is <= the frame size of the piece it derives from (each reframe <= the feed short, the feed short <= the master).

verifiers_auto.text: No crop or knockout tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry, and every downscaled entry is transcribed in the delivery note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the tradeoffs objects captured from every image call against the resize table in the note: assert every tradeoffs object reports upscale_factor <= 1.0 (crop_and_resize silently interpolates up to a 2x cap and reports it only inside tradeoffs), and assert every entry whose scale factor is < 1.0 appears verbatim in the note's resize table with its source asset named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion work, which are raster work, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
Whether the audio is treated as one file or as two populations, narration and demonstration, and where evenness is judged once it is two.
How much of the mic move can be reconciled before the two halves start sounding processed against each other.
Which segments the short has to carry, given that the host's notes and the episode disagree about both the verdict order and how many segments there are, and how to raise that with him.
How to frame a three way shootout upright and square when the ceiling is set by what the cut returned rather than by the 4K master.
Whether the host's chosen thumbnail select can actually carry a thumbnail, and how to say so if it cannot.
Knockout route on the holding shot: a subject cut, or a material-named ground selection inverted and filled, decided by what the wall shares with the subject.
How the bug is prepared for tracing, since raster preparation is the only lever the tracing tool has, and what to deliver for placements below the size the vector holds.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a credible independent reviewer, plus what the sponsor's named family actually resolves to and what to do about it.
Whether the card measure is set from the short lines or from the disclosure line that cannot be shortened.
Which stills join the grid and which are named as duplicates or soft rather than shipped.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image or video model and it returns generic tech-review-looking footage, a generic thumbnail and a generic bolt logo. IDENTITY: this is this channel's actual episode with its actual host, its actual three units and its actual verdict, the thumbnail is a specific frame the host chose of himself, and the bug must be reproduced from the channel's own file rather than redrawn, because a regenerated bolt is a different channel. SPEC: the short must be a genuine reduction of a specific twelve minute master, the reframes must not be enlarged, the sponsor's disclosure line must appear word for word, and the sponsor's name must be in a specific cut of a specific family, none of which a generated piece satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the card set is defined by being editable, because the host publishes several times a week and currently rebuilds these from scratch every episode. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the fan ramp survive the speech treatment, did the knockout bite the handle, does the bug still have counters at the size it prints.
doability_proof: Every link is drawn from CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account) and the standing DOABLE list, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. MOTION: video_create_quick_cut only ever SHORTENS, which is why the short is a reduction rather than an assembly, video_resize never enlarges, which is why the reframe ceiling is real, and media_summarize and media_enhance_speech are the summary and speech surfaces; these run on the connector's submit-and-resolve path and no gate in this task depends on measuring a frame or a waveform, only on watching and listening to what came back. No timestamp trimming, no format conversion and no frame extraction is used anywhere, so the thumbnail comes from the supplied selects rather than from the video. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: selection masks come back fully binary so any edge softness must come from remove_background's alpha, image_vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL so all tuning must happen in the raster prep, its output carries NO viewBox and an opaque full-canvas path at index zero, alpha survives crops at outputFileType png, and crop_and_resize will silently interpolate up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside tradeoffs. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, an inline SVG must sit in a wrapper with explicit left, top, width and height or its contents run off the canvas, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why the bug is audited from the returned per-card markup on every card. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: find_fonts FAMILY-NAME LOOKUP RETURNS AN ARBITRARY STYLE rather than the regular cut, get_fontkit_embed_url is case-sensitive and all-or-nothing, numeric weights are non-standard per family, and the CSS must use the returned slug, all verified; the sponsor's named face rides directly on those findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returns a real camera-scale JPEG, and boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and a partial success reported as a success. AVOIDED: no animate_design, no fill_text, no video_render or video_render_frame, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
